Connector.description:
A connector of the workspace: an integration of the catalog, installed
in one scope under one name, which a contract grants tools of.

integration.description: The id of the integration the connector installs: an entry of the workspace's catalog (`GET .../integrations`, then `GET .../integrations/{integration_id}`).
integration.title: Integration

name.description: The connector's name in the workspace, unique there: ASCII letters and digits, two of them joined by one `_` at most, e.g. `notion` or `notion_eu`. Tools are named after it, so the integration's longest tool name caps it: an integration may allow fewer than 32 characters, and a create or a rename over its cap is a 422 that says how many it allows.
name.title: Name

scope.description: Whose connection it holds: `shared`, one connection the whole workspace shares, or `personal`, each member's own.
scope.title: Scope

Connector.title: Connector

ConnectorApiKey.description: That a connector holds a key, and since when; never the key.

updated_at.description: When the key was last set.
updated_at.title: Updated At

api_key.description: The key, as the provider issued it; `user:password` for a connector that signs in with basic auth. Checked with the provider before it is stored when the provider has a check, and never answered.
api_key.title: Api Key

Contract.description:
A contract of the workspace: its identity and whether it is on. What it
grants, while it is on, is its latest version
(`GET /contracts/{contract_id}/versions/current`).

access_requests_enabled.description: Whether the contract's members may ask for more access from their AI client or the app. Applies at once. Changing it needs access requests on for the workspace.
access_requests_enabled.title: Access Requests Enabled

description.description: What the contract is for. Null or left out, none.
description.title: Description

enabled.description: Whether the contract is on. Off, its agents stay but are blocked, and a version created is stored without going in force; back on, its latest version is in force again. A contract with no version grants nothing either way.
enabled.title: Enabled

name.description: The contract's name, as its members see it.
name.title: Name

Integration.description:
An entry of the catalog the workspace sees, which a connector
installs in the workspace.

auth_type.description: How a connector of it signs in to the integration, as the catalog records it, e.g. `oauth`, `api_key` or `none`.
auth_type.title: Auth Type

description.description: What the integration does; empty when the catalog says nothing.
description.title: Description

id.description: The integration's id: what a connector's `integration` names.
id.title: Id

kind.description: How Hodor reaches it: `mcp`, an MCP server, or `api_wrapper`, an HTTP API Hodor serves as tools.
kind.title: Kind

name.description: The integration's name, as the catalog shows it.
name.title: Name

scopes.description: The scopes a connector of it may take, from `shared` and `personal`.
scopes.title: Scopes

slug.description: The integration's slug in the catalog, e.g. `notion`, the prefix of its tools' names. Answered only: a connector names its integration by `id`.
slug.title: Slug

tools.description: The names of its tools in the catalog, in the catalog's order: the version every connector starts from, before a connection brings its own.
tools.title: Tools

items.title: Items

slug.description: The integration's slug in the catalog, e.g. `notion`, the prefix of its tools' names. Answered only: a connector names its integration by `id`.

PermissionSet.description:
What a version opens on one connector: the tools it enables there. Its
mode follows the connector's scope.

connector_id.description: The connector the permission set opens, `con_...`.
connector_id.title: Connector Id

tools.description: The names of the connector's tools the permission set enables, as the integration lists them; at least one. A tool the connector exposes later is not enabled: there is no "all tools".
tools.title: Tools

PermissionSet.title: PermissionSet

Problem.description:
An error, as Problem Details (RFC 9457). `type` is a stable URI a client
tests against: it never changes for a given error. `title` belongs to the
type; `detail` explains this occurrence.

detail.description: What went wrong with this request, in English.
detail.title: Detail

errors.description: The parts of the request that were refused, on a `validation-failed` error.
errors.title: Errors

status.description: The HTTP status code of the response.
status.title: Status

title.description: A short summary of the kind of error.
title.title: Title

type.description: A URI that identifies the kind of error, e.g. `https://api.hodor.ai/problems/not-found`, or `about:blank` for an HTTP status with no type of its own.
type.title: Type

Problem.title: Problem

ProblemFieldError.description:
One part of the request the façade refused: where it is and why, never
the value sent, which may be a secret.

loc.description: Where the error is: `body`, `path` or `query`, then the field's path.
loc.title: Loc

msg.description: Why the value was refused, in English.
msg.title: Msg

type.description: The kind of error, e.g. `missing` or `string_too_long`.
type.title: Type

ProblemFieldError.title: ProblemFieldError

info.description: The API Hodor promises never to break, for clients Hodor does not run, the Terraform provider first. It takes a workspace API key and nothing else, and acts on the key's workspace. Every error is Problem Details (RFC 9457) with a stable `type`.

get.description:
The key's workspace: its id, which every public path starts with,
its name and when it was created.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

post.description:
A new connector of an integration the workspace's catalog holds. A
name the workspace already holds is a 409, a name longer than the
integration allows a 422 that says how long it may be.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

Location.description: The path of the new resource, from `/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}`.

delete.description:
Removes the connector with every connection of it, workspace and
personal, and its place in every contract that grants it.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

patch.description:
Renames the connector in place; its tools are named after it. A name
the workspace already holds is a 409, a name longer than the integration
allows a 422 that says how long it may be.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

put.description:
Sets the API key a shared connector calls its provider with:
`201` when it held none, `200` when this one replaces its key. The key is
checked with the provider first when the provider has a check (a refused
key is a 400, the provider out of reach a 502 or 504), and never answered.
A personal connector, or one that takes no key (it connects with
OAuth, or with no secret), is a 409.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

post.description:
A new contract, authored by the key's author. It grants nothing until
a version of it is created, which goes in force at once if the contract
is on (`enabled`, on by default); a refusal creates nothing. Audited
once, as the key: `contract.created`, with the contract's name and the
names of the fields the create set otherwise than a new contract reads
(`fields`, `access_requests_enabled` and `enabled` switched off).

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

Location.description: The path of the new resource, from `/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}`.

delete.description:
Deletes the contract, its versions and the agents it made; pending
access requests on it are cancelled.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

patch.description:
Changes what the body names, at once: a contract's identity is not
versioned. `enabled: false` blocks its agents and takes its version out
of force; `true` puts its latest version back in force, a 409 when that
version names a connector or a policy the workspace no longer has.
Audited as the key: a switch that puts a version in force or takes it
out is `contract.published` or `contract.unpublished`, and every other
field changed is named in one `contract.edited`.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

post.description:
A new version of the contract, whole, in force at once: the latest
version is the one in force, and the contract grants what it says from
this answer on. On a contract switched off, it is stored and goes in
force when the contract is switched on. A rollback is a new version with an older configuration.
It keeps the workspace policies the latest version attaches. A connector
removed while it is created is a 409 naming it; a policy it keeps, deleted
since, is a 409 too, which names none. A refusal writes nothing.

parameters.description: The workspace the key belongs to (`ws_...`). Any other answers 404.
parameters.name: workspace_id

Location.description: The path of the new resource, from `/v2/workspaces/{workspace_id}`.
